transcript.display:
### Understanding your situation
In March 2024 in Lucknow, a man took ₹2,00,000 from you promising a government job and disappeared. You have not yet filed an FIR, but you possess UPI screenshots and his phone number as evidence.

### Where you stand legally
- Because the incident occurred in March 2024, which is before 1 July 2024, your case falls under the Indian Penal Code, 1860 for cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property. [1]
- The offence of cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property carries a punishment of imprisonment up to seven years and a fine. [1]
- You have the right to report information about this cognizable offence to the officer in charge of a police station to have an FIR recorded, and you must be given a free copy. [2]

### Your options
1. **Police Complaint / FIR** — Go to the local police station in Lucknow to report the crime under Section 154 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for an official investigation into the cheating. [2][1]
2. **Superintendent of Police Complaint** — If the police station officer refuses to record your information, you may send the information in writing to the Superintendent of Police. [2]

### What to do next
1. Prepare a written complaint detailing how the man took ₹2,00,000 in March 2024 promising a government job and then disappeared.
2. Print out your UPI screenshots and note down his phone number clearly.
3. Visit the local police station in Lucknow to file your FIR under Section 154.
4. Obtain and keep safe a free copy of the recorded FIR from the police officer.
5. If the police station refuses to record your complaint, send a written complaint to the Superintendent of Police.

### Keep these ready
- UPI screenshots showing the transfer of ₹2,00,000
- The man's phone number
- Any chat history or call logs if available

### Draft: Police complaint (edit before using)
> To,
> The Officer in Charge,
> [Local Police Station Name],
> Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh.
>
> Subject: Complaint regarding cheating and fraudulent taking of money for a government job.
>
> Respected Sir/Madam,
>
> I am a resident of Lucknow. In March 2024, a man whose phone number is [Man's Phone Number] approached me and promised to secure a government job for me. Trusting his promise, I paid him a sum of ₹2,00,000 through UPI.
>
> After taking the money, the said person has disappeared and is not reachable. I have attached the UPI payment screenshots and his phone number as evidence of the transaction.
>
> I request you to register an FIR under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, investigate the matter, and take strict legal action against the accused.
>
> Sincerely,
> [Your Name]
> [Your Contact Information]

### When to involve a lawyer
- Criminal matters can affect your liberty and record; have a lawyer review the complaint or FIR before you file or respond.
- Free legal aid: NALSA helpline **15100**, or your District Legal Services Authority (DLSA).

### Assumptions and gaps
- It is assumed the exact date in March 2024 is not formally documented beyond the month itself, and no subsequent threats or breaches of trust occurred beyond the initial cheating.

---
**Sources (Bare Act provisions)**
1. Section 420, *Indian Penal Code, 1860* — Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property (offences before 1 July 2024)
2. Section 154, *Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973* — FIR under the older procedure law (offences before 1 July 2024)
